description: Second scenario for the same requirement: after an InstallSnapshot leaves a log tail above the snapshot index, an AppendEntries anchored at the snapshot index must still be accepted, so the follower can resume replicating from the leader; instead the handler rejects it because the effective last entry comes from the retained tail and the log no longer holds the anchor.

harness.description: TestAssuranceInstallSnapshotTailReplacedByAppendEntries seeds a log through index 5, installs a snapshot at index 3 through the production handler, reports the retained tail, then delivers the AppendEntries a leader would send next - anchored at the snapshot index with entries conflicting with the tail - and reports whether it was accepted, the resulting last entry, term and commit index.
semantic_changes: installSnapshot and appendEntries are invoked directly on their main-thread code paths because skipStartup leaves no main loop; in production processRPC dispatches both from the transport consumer channel.
An explicit substitute goroutine answers restore futures with success because runFSM is not running; it never inspects or modifies log, snapshot or term state.

The log content is written to the caller-owned LogStore before NewRaft and the snapshot payload is synthetic because the harness FSM ignores content; conf.TrailingLogs is 0 so compaction runs at the snapshot index.

legality.derivation: S57 shows the receive path adopting the snapshot index and compacting without setting the last log; S58 shows the compaction bound removes entries through the snapshot index; S54 shows the effective last entry is the maximum of log and snapshot position, so with a retained tail the anchor index differs from it; S8 shows that the AppendEntries previous-log check falls back to the log store whenever the anchor is not the effective last entry and rejects with NoRetryBackoff when the entry cannot be read. The chain from the misalignment to the rejection is therefore sourced.
legality.applicability: Applies to a receiver that installed a snapshot and retained log entries above the installed index, and is then sent the entries a leader provides after a successful install (nextIndex = snapshot index + 1).
unresolved: Whether a real leader drives a follower into the retained-tail state; the check seeds it.
What the leader does next (decrementing nextIndex and possibly re-sending a snapshot) was not measured; the check reports the receiver's decision only.
alternatives: If the retained tail is always replaced before the leader's next AppendEntries, the rejection would not be reachable in a deployment.

grounding.derivation: S57 locates the missing alignment step, S54 explains why the anchor differs from the effective last entry once a tail is retained, and S8 shows the check that then fails. The event reports whether the leader's next AppendEntries was accepted.
grounding.applicability: Evaluated only when the install retained a tail above the installed index, which the prerequisite declares.

observable_properties.description: After an InstallSnapshot that retained a tail, an AppendEntries anchored at the snapshot index is accepted, so replication can resume from the installed snapshot.

uncertainties: Real-leader reachability of the retained-tail state.
The leader's subsequent behaviour (nextIndex decrement, repeated snapshots) was not measured.
Whether the rejection is transient in a deployment depends on the same premise.
